status_note: The locked Ghidra oracle records the real Architecture-owned Database graph, lazy FunctionSymbol-owned Funcdata, Database-owned ScopeLocal alias identities, two distinct attachScope failure ownership contracts, and the destructor cascade. Both sides execute their real findCreateScope/find_create_scope path: the selected id/name/parent/repeat-key/cardinality projection matches, while the full case remains MISMATCH because Ghidra directly returns and owns Scope pointers and has no scope-id allocator counter, whereas Rugra returns u64, stores Scope values and child ids, and advances next_scope_id. Rugra's post-lookup slot equality is reported separately and is not presented as Ghidra return-object identity. Rugra also cannot express the caller-owned Scope identity input used by attachScope failures. No difference is normalized into a full function MATCH, and no covered mapping is promoted to L3.

rugra_source.snapshot_policy: Archive only the explicit crate closure from this commit and compile the live fixture as an overlay; never read live src/*.rs and never require runtime HEAD equality.

decisive_semantics.reference_output_parameters: Architecture::buildDatabase stores the new Database in Architecture::symboltab and returns the exact registered global Scope pointer. Ghidra Database::findCreateScope directly returns a Scope pointer from pointer-owned idmap/children, so resolver/repeat/parent-child aliases are compared to that return pointer. Rugra find_create_scope returns only u64 from a value-owned BTreeMap and child-id vector; its resolver and parent-child slots are compared exactly after lookup but are explicitly marked unavailable as direct return aliases. Raw pointer values are never printed. Database::attachScope stores the incoming caller-owned Scope pointer and sets its parent; FunctionSymbol::getFunction caches one Funcdata pointer; Funcdata stores the exact FunctionSymbol back-reference and exact Database-owned ScopeLocal pointer.
decisive_semantics.loop_bounds_traversal_order: Database::clearReferences recursively visits Scope::children from begin to end, both std::map<uint8,Scope*> order; ScopeInternal::~ScopeInternal walks every EntryMap then every SymbolNameTree element before Scope::~Scope walks remaining children. The sentinel destructor runs in the latter child phase and observes that FunctionSymbol::~FunctionSymbol -> Funcdata::~Funcdata -> Database::deleteScope has already detached the ScopeLocal.
decisive_semantics.counter_accumulator_lifecycle: The buildDatabase override counts invocations and requires exactly one. Both find-create paths insert the explicit id once and the repeat lookup neither creates a second scope nor replaces its name or parent, but only Rugra exposes and advances Database::next_scope_id from 1 to id+1 on creation; Ghidra Database has no corresponding counter field or mutation. ScopeInternal nextUniqueId is incremented only when addSymbolInternal assigns the FunctionSymbol id; FunctionSymbol::getFunction allocates only when fd is null and reuses it thereafter. Duplicate attach does not increment or replace any registered id, and both failure cases preserve the pre-existing Database state described by their records.
decisive_semantics.sorting_comparison_keys: Database::idmap and the Rugra Database scope map are keyed solely by uint8/u64 scope id; the first find-create lookup inserts id 0x12040002 and the second hits that key despite a different requested name. Ghidra Scope::children is an id-sorted map of Scope pointers, while Rugra Scope::children is an insertion-order Vec<u64>; this one-child projection records cardinality but leaves multi-child order UNTESTED. Duplicate detection uses idmap.insert before parent attachment; the unparented duplicate's getFullName is therefore the empty string, yielding the exact message 'Duplicate scope id: '. Symbol deletion uses SymbolNameTree order; the fixture installs one FunctionSymbol so there is no unobserved equal-key tie.

analysis_options.architecture_constructor: FixtureArchitecture derives from BfdArchitecture(examples/curl, default) only to override the protected virtual buildDatabase hook; the override calls the locked Architecture::buildDatabase body exactly once and records its returned aliases. All other initialization is BfdArchitecture::init.
analysis_options.symbol_loading: readLoaderSymbols is not called. The namespace, FunctionSymbol, and Funcdata use artificial RAM addresses 0x7e120400 and 0x7e120500 after normal x86-64 spec initialization, so loader-symbol contents cannot affect the ownership records.
analysis_options.api: Architecture::buildDatabase; Database::{attachScope,findCreateScope,resolveScope,deleteScope}; Rugra Database::find_create_scope; Scope::{addFunction,removeSymbol,resolveScope}; FunctionSymbol::{getFunction,~FunctionSymbol}; Funcdata::{Funcdata,~Funcdata,getScopeLocal}; ScopeLocal::ScopeLocal; ScopeInternal::~ScopeInternal; Scope::~Scope
analysis_options.error_injection: A second non-global Scope with id 0x12040001 exercises duplicate-id RecovError after idmap.insert fails. A fresh Database receives a name-bearing root Scope to exercise invalid-global-name LowlevelError before global assignment. ProbeScope destructors distinguish callee-deleted from caller-owned incoming objects.
analysis_options.destructor_probe: The exit graph has one namespace FunctionSymbol/Funcdata/ScopeLocal plus an independent sentinel child. Architecture destruction deletes Database before prototype models/types/translator; Database deletes global; namespace ScopeInternal deletes its FunctionSymbol, which deletes Funcdata, which detaches/deletes ScopeLocal; only then Scope::~Scope deletes the sentinel. The sentinel queries its still-live parent by local name and records local_present=0.
analysis_options.rugra_projection: The Rust executable calls the real Database::find_create_scope twice and observes its returned ids, exact resolved-slot equality after lookup, exact parent-child-resolved-slot equality, child count, stored name/parent, return/storage classes bound by compile-time helpers to the concrete production return/map/children types, and next_scope_id before/create/repeat state. It explicitly labels direct return-object aliases UNAVAILABLE because the production API returns u64. It separately constructs Architecture::new and Funcdata::new to observe their real empty ownership fields. It does not create ownership lookalikes or normalize the u64/value-owned/counter differences into the Ghidra graph.
analysis_options.debug_macros: OPACTION_DEBUG, CPUI_DEBUG, and CPUI_STATISTICS are absent.
analysis_options.normalization: No semantic difference is normalized. Raw addresses are fixed inputs; pointer addresses are deliberately replaced only by exact equality/null alias classes because allocation addresses are non-semantic. The find-create return/storage classes and Rugra-only next_scope_id mutation are emitted as explicit mismatches. Exception categories and text, map membership, parent/back-reference identities, child counts, and destructor event order remain observable. BfdArchitecture diagnostics are captured in an in-memory stream and both comparand stderr streams must be empty.
analysis_options.random_seed: none; construction, map traversal, failure paths, and output are deterministic

bfd.include_tree_hash_scheme: sha256 of bfd-include-tree-v1 plus sorted length-prefixed basenames and file contents

build_database_graph.ghidra_oracle_observation: MATCH: one call returns the exact global registered in the new Database; Database and global both point back to the same Architecture; global is id 0, empty-named, parentless, and has no Funcdata back-reference.
build_database_graph.rugra_difference: Architecture::new leaves symboltab=None and the concrete Architecture has only an external set_symboltab seam; ArchitectureBuilder::build_database is an unimplemented trait hook.

full.reason: Ghidra returns and owns Scope pointers without a scope-id allocator mutation; Rugra returns u64, stores Scope values and child ids, and advances next_scope_id.

multi_child_order.reason: Only one child is created, so this fixture cannot compare Ghidra's id-sorted Scope* map traversal with Rugra's insertion-order u64 vector. The output is neither sorted nor normalized to imply coverage.

find_create_scope_projection.ghidra_oracle_observation: MATCH selected scalar/key projection: findCreateScope creates id 0x12040002 under global, repeat lookup preserves the key/name/parent, and child count is one. Full output: the API returns Scope*, and resolveScope, repeat return, plus the parent child table all alias that exact return pointer; Database idmap and Scope children own Scope* identities; no Database scope-id allocator counter exists.
find_create_scope_projection.rugra_observation: MATCH selected scalar/key projection: find_create_scope creates the same explicit id under parent 0, repeat lookup preserves the key/name/parent, and child count is one. Full output differs: the API returns u64, so direct return-object aliases are unavailable; post-lookup BTreeMap slot and child-id resolution equality are recorded separately and cannot prove Ghidra return identity. Compile-time helpers instantiated on the production types classify the return, scope-map storage, and child storage as values, versus pointers on Ghidra. Creation advances public next_scope_id from 1 to 302252035.
find_create_scope_projection.full_difference: Return type, direct return alias availability, stored ownership/reference representation, and the Rugra-only next_scope_id mutation are observable differences, so the complete function case is MISMATCH despite the matching selected projection. Multi-child traversal order is separately UNTESTED.

function_scope_ownership.ghidra_oracle_observation: MATCH: namespace, FunctionSymbol, cached Funcdata, Database-resolved ScopeLocal, parent, Architecture, and FunctionSymbol back-reference alias classes all have the locked values; ScopeLocal::isGlobal=false proves the Funcdata back-reference class.
function_scope_ownership.rugra_difference: FunctionSymbol has only Symbol/consume_size/entry; Funcdata::new has arch=None and scope=None; Database/Scope and varmap ScopeLocal remain distinct value-owned models.

attach_failure_ownership.ghidra_oracle_observation: MATCH: duplicate id throws RecovError('Duplicate scope id: '), deletes the incoming unparented Scope, and retains the original; invalid global name throws LowlevelError without taking/deleting the incoming Scope and leaves globalscope null.
attach_failure_ownership.rugra_difference: Database::find_create_scope proves that explicit-id creation and repeat identity lookup are present. The remaining mismatch is narrower: public Database APIs cannot receive a caller-owned Scope object identity or reproduce attachScope's callee-delete versus caller-retain exception ownership contracts.

destructor_cascade.ghidra_oracle_observation: MATCH: removing FunctionSymbol removes its mapping and synchronously deletes/detaches its ScopeLocal; full Architecture destruction enters namespace destruction, deletes FunctionSymbol/Funcdata/ScopeLocal, then deletes the sentinel child, which observes local_present=0.
destructor_cascade.rugra_difference: The split value/Arc models have no FunctionSymbol -> Funcdata -> Database-owned ScopeLocal destruction cascade to run on the same input.

remaining_branches.reason: Further find-create edges (explicit id below current next_scope_id, u64::MAX counter overflow, empty non-global name, a missing parent, and multiple-child traversal order: Ghidra id-sorted Scope* map versus Rugra insertion-order id vector); multiple-global-scope rejection; attachScope(non-global, empty-name) LowlevelError; duplicate IDs nested below a non-global parent; decode-created function scopes; Funcdata construction without a FunctionSymbol, including its address-derived local-scope id; FunctionSymbol destruction while its fd is still null; constructor attach failure after partial Funcdata initialization; deleteScope missing-parent-reference LowlevelError; multiple FunctionSymbols and symbol-name destructor ordering; and exception injection during nested clearReferences are outside this ten-record Ghidra/four-record Rugra fixture.
